TARGET ENGAGEMENT: There is evidence of target engagement with biomarker changes showing increased cycling CD8+ T cells (2.86% at 15mg, 10.26% at 25mg) and changes in T cell populations, indicating both PI3K inhibition and PD-1 blockade were active. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The biomarker data shows downstream immune activation with increased cycling CD8+ cells and effector memory T cells, confirming pathway modulation occurred. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Despite target engagement and pathway modulation, clinical endpoints failed - ORR was only 20% in the 15mg arm and 0% in the 25mg arm, with poor PFS (2.8-3.0 months) across both doses. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported to suggest differential responses. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial was severely limited by dose-limiting toxicity with 80% of patients experiencing grade 3+ treatment-related AEs, hepatic toxicity including hepatic failure (16.7%), transaminase elevations (85.7%), and two deaths in the 15mg arm. The sponsor discontinued support, likely due to the unfavorable risk-benefit profile.
